scores.claim_text: Mission Technology Solutions (MTS, formerly Government Solutions) generated $5,581 million in fiscal 2025 revenue (~72% of $7,786M total consolidated revenue) primarily serving U.S. DoW, intelligence community, NASA, U.K. MoD, and Australian defense customers.
supports: USAspending.query_dod_contracts: 2,043 DoD awards to KBR SERVICES LLC; cumulative obligated $43.8B across history. Confirms KBR is among the largest DoD logistics/services primes — segment scale of $5.58B/yr is consistent with a long-running, recurring DoD revenue base (LOGCAP V task orders, IDIQ vehicles).
Filing internally consistent: MTS $5,581M / total $7,786M = 71.7%; U.S. gov $4,427M = 56.9% of total.
scores.interpretation: Segment size and DoD-prime narrative corroborated by USAspending. No contradiction. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Sustainable Technology Solutions (STS) generated $2,205 million in fiscal 2025 revenue (~28% of total), up 2% from $2,155M, anchored by 85+ proprietary process technologies in ammonia/syngas, petrochemicals, clean refining, and circular-economy verticals.
supports: Out-of-scope for the J-Book / federal-contracting verifier suite — STS is commercial/industrial process licensing, not federal funded. No M-source contradiction.
Internally consistent (2,205/2,155 = +2.3% y/y, matches disclosed +2%; 2,205/7,786 = 28.3%).

M_value.note: commercial segment outside the catalog scope

scores.interpretation: Cannot adjudicate commercial process-licensing claims with federal contracting M-sources. Mark UNVERIFIABLE rather than passing without external corroboration.

scores.claim_text: U.S. government represented $4,427 million (57%) of fiscal 2025 consolidated revenues and U.K. government represented $663 million (9%); no other customer exceeded 10% threshold. U.S. government accounts receivable concentration is 47% of consolidated AR.
supports: revenue_concentration.query_revenue_concentration: returned UNVERIFIABLE because KBR discloses customer concentration (57% U.S. gov) but does NOT disclose top vehicle pct or top task-order pct — the verifier needs at least one of those for adjudication.

Peer-median context from the verifier: services-prime peer median top_customer_pct=86%, so KBR's 57% looks LESS concentrated than peers on the customer axis (i.e., KBR's commercial STS segment dilutes the federal concentration). Directionally favorable but not a formal PASS without vehicle disclosure.
Materiality: 57% to single customer (U.S. gov) is material but consistent with peers (LDOS/SAIC/BAH all 80%+); KBR is actually below peer median due to STS dilution.
scores.interpretation: KBR omits the vehicle/TO concentration disclosure that peers provide. UNVERIFIABLE under the verifier, but the disclosed customer concentration is BELOW peer median — actual concentration risk likely lower than typical defense prime.

scores.claim_text: KBR derives significant MTS revenue from U.S. intelligence community customers including National Reconnaissance Office, National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency, and 'other intelligence agencies' under classified work requiring cleared personnel and facility clearances.
supports: ic_contracting_proxy.query_ic_revenue_consistency: UNVERIFIABLE — KBR does NOT disclose either (a) a dollar IC revenue figure or (b) cleared-employee count in the 10-K Human Capital section. Filing references 'individuals with high-level security clearance' qualitatively but provides no number.

10-K discloses ~36,000 total employees across 28 countries but does NOT break out the cleared subset. LinQuest acquisition (Aug 2024) is described as bringing 'defense and intel programs' growth, qualitatively supporting IC exposure.

USAspending DoD flow ($43.8B lifetime, $8.95B top task order under LOGCAP) is dominated by Army logistics, not IC agencies — IC awards are typically classified and would not appear in USAspending DoD pull.

M_value.gap: no cleared headcount in Human Capital section

scores.interpretation: KBR's IC claim cannot be benchmarked without cleared headcount disclosure. Note: this is a material disclosure gap relative to pure-play IC primes (CACI, SAIC, LDOS) which disclose cleared FTE counts.

scores.claim_text: Cyber analytics and cybersecurity are described as a core MTS capability area; KBR positions itself in 'cyber analytics, cybersecurity, space and air dominance, connected battlespace, national security intelligence' work for DoW and IC customers.
supports: cybercom_budget.query_cybercom_envelope: FY2025 envelope $1.94B, FY2026 $1.96B — FUNDED_STEADY (slight growth). Cyber addressable market for DoD primes is funded and growing modestly.
Claim is descriptive/capability-level (not a specific contract), and the broader cyber budget envelope supports the narrative.
scores.interpretation: Cyber capability claim is a small (<5%) line for KBR but supported by steady cyber funding envelope. PASS.

scores.claim_text: Backlog of unfulfilled orders was $16,864 million as of January 2, 2026 (up from $16,605M y/y), with approximately 36% expected to convert to revenue in fiscal 2026 and 17% held within equity-method joint ventures (Aspire Defence, Affinity/MFTS, JKC, KZJV).
supports: pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding: probed Aspire Defence, LogCAP, Affinity, MFTS — all NOT_FOUND in J-Book corpus (Aspire/MFTS are UK MoD programs, outside U.S. J-Book scope; LogCAP is O&M, not RDT&E line item).

Backlog growth is only 1.6% y/y ($16,864 vs $16,605M) which is BELOW MTS revenue book-to-bill needed to sustain mid-single-digit growth. Combined with MTS organic revenue shrinkage (see C8), this is a flat-to-soft backlog signal.
36% expected to convert in fiscal 2026 implies ~$6.1B revenue, consistent with run-rate, but no acceleration.

M_value.interp: UK PFI programs and O&M IDIQs not in RDT&E J-Book

scores.interpretation: Backlog growth is anemic (+1.6% y/y) at a defense services prime nominally pursuing 'defense modernization' growth vectors. Not RED, but warrants MODERATE flag — investors should not extrapolate aggressive growth from this backlog trajectory.

scores.claim_text: Defense modernization, national security space superiority, and hypersonics test & evaluation are named strategic growth vectors and KBR claims long-term programs in defense modernization and space superiority funded by U.S. DoW and allied governments.
supports: pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding('space superiority'): FUNDED_STEADY — Space Superiority ISR (PE 1203330SF, Space Force) funded $28.7M FY24 → $24.4M FY26. Program exists and is funded though small.

pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding('hypersonics test and evaluation'): NOT_FOUND — no matching line item in corpus. KBR does not name a specific PE for hypersonics T&E; cohort note mentioned it but filing only references it as a generic growth vector.

pentagon_jbook.query_program_funding('defense modernization'): NOT_FOUND — generic vector, no specific PE. Pattern-of-disclosure issue: KBR uses growth-vector language rather than naming PEs/contracts.
scores.interpretation: Space Superiority ISR is funded and steady, supporting the broad space-growth claim. The other two vectors are generic and lack PE-level support, but materiality is low because KBR doesn't quantify revenue contribution from any of these vectors. PASS on the only PE-resolvable claim.

scores.claim_text: KBR's MTS growth in fiscal 2025 was driven by the August 2024 LinQuest acquisition (defense and intel programs) and the May 2025 Infrastar acquisition; offset by 'reduced activity within the European command and science and space programs' indicating organic MTS revenue shrinkage ex-M&A.
supports: Filing self-discloses: MTS +$26M = +0.5% y/y INCLUDING a full year of LinQuest (acquired Aug-2024, so FY25 was first full year). LinQuest deal was valued at ~$737M (per FY24 disclosure); even at ~10% LinQuest growth, the LinQuest contribution alone would be $300-500M of incremental revenue. Implied organic MTS shrinkage: high single digits / low double digits.
Also disclosed: $26M FY24 favorable legacy-claim resolution that did NOT recur in FY25 (i.e., FY24 base was inflated, making FY25 growth optically better than underlying).
USAspending DoD flow shows historical LOGCAP-era concentration — current contract base is in run-off (LogCAP III still in closeout per Item 14). Forward DoD pipeline replacing legacy O&M is unclear.
Cohort context: KBR announced MTS spin-off in September 2025 targeting H2 fiscal 2026 — strategic admission that MTS is not adding value to consolidated multiple.
scores.M_check: usaspending.query_dod_contracts (cross-referenced with disclosed M&A and segment build)
scores.interpretation: MODERATE — when LinQuest annualization and the $26M legacy-claim non-recurrence are stripped out, the organic MTS business shrank in fiscal 2025. The September 2025 spin-off announcement supports this interpretation. Not RED (still funded and operating), but the 'defense modernization growth' narrative is undermined by the math.

summary.j_book_hits: pentagon_jbook fired on 3 of 8 claims (C5/cybercom, C6, C7); 1 PE-level match (Space Superiority ISR PE 1203330SF FUNDED_STEADY)
